content.text: I found the sourcing and ingestion services still using those files. I’ll stop only those local processes first, then remove the verified dataset directories and clear the active approvals.

These processes belong to the project’s single local startup stack, which automatically shuts down the whole stack if one service stops. I’m stopping it cleanly to prevent the ingestion worker from recreating or touching files during deletion; it can be restarted afterward with the normal startup script.

Deleted from your local machine:

- ~47 GB ingestion cache, extracted files, and TimeF output
- Ingestion database
- Both active approved-source entries

The local Trace stack was stopped safely. No code changed. Deleted dataset files require re-downloading to recover.
I already merged the PR. But I was thinking, maybe user should be able to approve more than one candidate after a sourcing run.

Yes—approval should be a per-candidate action, so one sourcing run can add several reviewed candidates to the approved library. I’ll inspect the merged implementation and its frontend/API contracts, then extend it without changing the one-time ingestion rule. I’m using the interface-design, frontend, incremental-implementation, and git-workflow skills because this spans a user flow and its backend contract.

The merged backend currently makes the first approval terminal and stores only one manifest per run. I’m keeping that first approval backward-compatible, then allowing additional eligible candidates to be approved from the completed run. Each extra approval will remain independently auditable and appear in the same approved-source library; rejected or gate-failing candidates will still be blocked.
